title: 2 Thessalonians Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on 2 Thessalonians 3: the request for prayer, the example of working night and day, and what to do with the disorderly.

questions.text: What do they ask the readers to pray for?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 asks them to pray that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, as it also did with them.

answers.text: That the letter may reach Macedonia
That their journey may be short
That the assembly may grow rich
That the word of the Lord may spread rapidly

questions.text: From whom do they ask to be delivered, according to verse 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 asks that they may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men, for not all have faith.

answers.text: Idle brothers and busybodies
Unreasonable and evil men
The rulers of the city
Those who ask for bread

questions.text: What will the faithful Lord do, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says the Lord is faithful, who will establish them and guard them from the evil one.

answers.text: Repay those who afflict them
Send them help from Athens
Guard them from the evil one
Shorten the days of trouble

questions.text: Into what is the Lord asked to direct their hearts?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 asks the Lord to direct their hearts into God's love and into the perseverance of Christ.

answers.text: Into God's love and the perseverance of Christ
Into the fear of the coming judgment
Into the keeping of the whole law
Into the hope of relief from affliction

questions.text: From whom are they commanded to withdraw themselves?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 commands them to withdraw from every brother who walks in rebellion, and not after the tradition they received.

answers.text: Everyone who is outside the faith
Every brother who walks in rebellion
Everyone who is poor and asks bread
Everyone who teaches in the assembly

questions.text: What do they say about the bread they ate while among them?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says they did not eat bread from anyone's hand without paying for it, but worked night and day.

answers.text: The elders provided it
They ate no bread at all
The assembly gave it freely
They paid for it

questions.text: Why did they work instead of using their right?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says it was not because they don't have the right, but to make themselves an example that the readers should imitate.

answers.text: To make themselves an example
Because the assembly was poor
Because no one offered them food
Because the law required it

questions.text: What command had they already given when they were with them?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 recalls the command: “If anyone is not willing to work, don't let him eat.”

answers.text: Whoever does not pray should not teach
Whoever is idle should leave the city
Whoever is not willing to work should not eat
Whoever has bread should give it away

questions.text: What does verse 11 say about some who walk among them in rebellion?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says they don't work at all, but are busybodies.

answers.text: They teach a different doctrine
They take payment for preaching
They have left the assembly
They don't work, but are busybodies

questions.text: How should the one who doesn't obey this letter be treated?
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 say to have no company with him, that he may be ashamed, and not to count him as an enemy but to admonish him as a brother.

answers.text: As an enemy to be driven out
As a brother to be admonished
As one who was never in the faith
As a teacher to be followed
